name: Charles IV crowned Holy Roman Emperor in Rome
summary: Charles IV is crowned emperor at St Peter's by a papal legate (the popes still resident at Avignon). The Roman expedition is brief and ceremonial; Charles immediately returns north and the following year promulgates the Golden Bull of 1356 codifying imperial election procedure.

_quarry.structural_significance: Last German emperor to receive coronation in Rome during the Avignon papacy; the Golden Bull that follows fixes the seven electors and removes papal involvement in imperial elections, ending centuries of papal-imperial dispute over the procedure.
